report.source_text: A cervical lymph node biopsy and medullary femur biopsy confirmed nodular sclerosing classic Hodgkin lymphoma. Microscopic findings included sclerotic bands causing lymph node effacement and large, atypical, multinucleated cells with prominent eosinophilic nucleoli (figure 1). Immunohistochemical staining demonstrated positivity to CD15 and CD30 with negative staining for CD45.

report.source_text: Total bilirubin peaked at 21.7 a few days after the second dose of BV-PC then down trended to 12 mg/dL, at which point the patient was started on a modified brentuximab vedotin, doxorubicin, vincristine, etoposide, prednisone and cyclophosphamide (Bv-AVE-PC) protocol. Prednisolone 35 mg was also given two times per day for 7 days at the start of cycles 1–3. This was the same as used in the ongoing Children’s Oncology Group Phase 3 study AHOD 1331 though it was 50% dose reduced for decreased liver function for cycle 1 and then increased to 75% for cycles 2–5.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Vanishing bile duct syndrome (VBDS) in a patient presenting with classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A male in his 20s presented with acute jaundice, abdominal pain, and nausea superimposed on 6 months of intermittent fevers and 10 kg weight loss. Initial evaluation revealed severe cholestasis (total bilirubin 10.9 mg/dL, direct 8.5 mg/dL, ALP 941 U/L) with systemic inflammation. Imaging demonstrated a patent biliary tree without obstruction. Cervical lymph node and femur biopsies confirmed nodular sclerosing classical Hodgkin lymphoma (CD15+, CD30+, CD45-). Liver biopsy revealed portal tract inflammation with focal small bile duct destruction and dropout, F0 fibrosis, and CK7 stain confirming small bile duct obliteration without Reed-Sternberg cells, findings highly suggestive of VBDS. Extensive serologic workup excluded viral hepatitis (HBV, HCV, CMV, EBV), autoimmune liver disease (ANA, AMA, ASMA negative), and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. The patient received initial symptomatic treatment with ursodeoxycholic acid and prednisolone, followed by modified Bv-AVE-PC chemotherapy (dose-reduced for hepatic dysfunction). Bilirubin peaked at 21.7 mg/dL but downtrended to 12 mg/dL with treatment initiation and eventually normalized to 1.7 mg/dL by 19 months post-admission, with complete metabolic response of lymphoma on imaging.
